races.name: Sharon Pardy 60th Birthday Celebration Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 5yo has won twice from seven starts on similar going and comfortably fills the front-running role here; Miss Heidi Palin claims 5lb and the STYLE_FIT tag is a mild flag given she is not quite stepping into a foreign role, but the combination of pace-setting and course suitability is strong.

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Four wins from his last four completed starts on good ground is a striking sequence, and Harry Atkins's 5lb claim adds value — the hood (headgear: p) suggests a horse that needs assistance to focus, but his jumping and prominently-ridden style suit a race run at a controlled clip with a clear target to attack.

runners_data.name: He's Tailor Made
runners_data.note: Explicitly tagged as a horse who fades in the finish, and his last three form figures of 8, 5, and 10 on good ground paint a consistent picture of a horse who gets outpaced late; Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim does not change the profile here, and the 2m½f on fast ground looks a genuine stamina test he may not be equipped for.

runners_data.name: Obsessedwithyou
runners_data.note: Gavin Sheehan rides a horse with an outstanding 15-from-15 record on similar going — the quality is undeniable — but her natural front-running style has been redistributed to midfield because Loriko fills that berth; she will need to overcome a positional concession that sits at odds with how her best form has been produced.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: A pull-up sits in recent form alongside a second at 16f on good ground, making her a horse of inconsistent reliability; Nick Slatter's 3lb claim is the lowest allowance in the race and she is a hold-up type whose best chance rests on a compressed or chaotic finish that her profile alone cannot manufacture.

races.paceDynamic: Loriko is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners in a novice hurdle over 2m½f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop entirely unchallenged for the lead. Edelak and Obsessedwithyou are both naturally prominent types, but with Loriko already filling that role, the field holds more front-running and prominent horses than can all occupy their preferred position — Loriko and Edelak, trained together by Dan Skelton, are best placed to secure the front two slots, with Obsessedwithyou likely squeezed into a midfield berth against her natural inclinations. The result is a measured, controlled tempo set by Loriko that will not burn off the field early, leaving this as a race likely to be decided by jumping fluency and acceleration from the second-last — a shape that strongly favours horses who travel prominently and can quicken from a stalking position off a genuine but uncontested pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Loriko Controls, Skelton Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko dictates an uncontested lead and Edelak tracks in her slipstream throughout, the Dan Skelton yard turns this into a two-horse procession.
scenarios.body: Loriko sets a measured pace on ground she handles well, and Edelak — with four wins from his last four completed hurdle starts — sits primed to challenge from the second-last; both horses travel prominently, which is exactly the profile this race shape rewards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Obsessedwithyou Finds Rhythm
scenarios.trigger: If Obsessedwithyou, despite being squeezed from her natural front position, settles quickly and recovers ground from the third-last to mount a late prominent challenge.
scenarios.body: Her exceptional form record — five wins and eleven places from fifteen good-ground starts — gives her the class to overcome positional compromise, and if the pace is steady enough she can close from midfield as she did when winning at 16f on good going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late or jumping errors disrupt the front two, a hold-up horse benefits from a compressed finish.
scenarios.body: Angel Of My Dreams has placed on good ground over 16f but her form string of 08-2P4 suggests inconsistency, and He's Tailor Made is explicitly flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — neither is a reliable closer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make significant jumping errors or the race breaks up dramatically from an early incident, the form book is disrupted.
scenarios.body: He's Tailor Made has struggled badly in similar conditions and Angel Of My Dreams has a pull-up in recent form, so this is a field with fragile horses who could fall out of contention — but the beneficiary would most likely still be one of the Skelton pair given their jumping form.

watchPoints.text: Edelak's jumping is the pivotal factor — if he travels fluently behind Loriko and pings the second-last, he has the form and trainer momentum to take this race away from the field.

Obsessedwithyou's inability to get her natural prominent pitch is the key positional risk to monitor; if she is restless or unbalanced in midfield in the early stages, Gavin Sheehan will face a difficult decision whether to push forward or absorb the traffic.
He's Tailor Made's tendency to fade in the finish means he is a horse to watch as a potential jumping hazard to horses around him from the third-last onwards if he begins to tire.

The Dan Skelton yard is running two horses in the same race (Loriko and Edelak) from a 6/21 fortnight strike rate — stable form is good and it is worth noting whether both are ridden to win or whether one is an intended pacemaker for the other.

Good-to-firm conditions at Stratford are confirmed for this race, and every runner in the field is marked going=OK — but Angel Of My Dreams has only one placed run from five starts on similar ground, making her going profile the weakest of any horse here despite the neutral tag.

races.name: George & Dragon Novices' Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Duel Au Soleil
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter with a clear lead role; Ben Pauling's yard is winless from three over the last 14 days but the horse's recent placed form on good and soft ground (1W4P in similar conditions) and OR 111 mark gives him strong claims if he dictates uncontested; tongue-tie and visor noted, 18 days since last run.

runners_data.name: The Long Walk
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a wide-margin second at 2m6f on good ground last time representing the Jonjo/A.J. O'Neill combination, who are firing 3/13 over the past fortnight; the 43-day absence is worth monitoring but his stamina profile suits this longer trip if the pace collapses in the home straight.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwaitingfor
runners_data.note: Charlie Longsdon's five-year-old boasts an excellent placed record — eight places from 12 on similar ground — and has the consistent profile to capitalise if Duel Au Soleil weakens; races prominently as his natural style and should have no difficulty securing the position directly behind the leader from the start.

runners_data.name: Mary
runners_data.note: In reality a front-running or prominent-style horse whose true racing style cannot be deployed in this shape because the two natural pace-setters ahead of her are better placed to claim those positions; Ian Williams has two wins from 30 over 14 days, and her good-ground form at 2m (five runs, 2W8P) is solid, but racing out of character limits her chance here.

runners_data.name: Hooper
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type with headgear (tongue-tie) who has recorded zero wins from 15 similar-ground starts; the claiming allowance from Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell (7lb) helps offset the OR 103 mark, but his Stratford form and age make him the most speculative runner in the field if the pace doesn't set up perfectly for a late charge.

races.paceDynamic: Duel Au Soleil is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo on good to firm ground at Stratford. Whatyouwaitingfor will push forward to sit just off the pace in a prominent berth, while The Long Walk and Hooper will be held up in the rear, likely tracking the two leaders from a short distance. Mary is a natural prominent type who cannot find that position in this shape — Duel Au Soleil and Whatyouwaitingfor have first claim on the front two slots, leaving Mary to race out of character in a midfield role. This field holds more genuine prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, and it is Duel Au Soleil and Whatyouwaitingfor who are most likely to actually secure their preferred positions. A steady-to-moderate gallop set by a single, uncontested pace-setter over this trip on good to firm ground classically suits a prominent racer who can race handily throughout and out-jump the hold-up horses in the home straight — the race shape strongly favours those able to travel close to the pace from the outset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Duel Au Soleil Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Duel Au Soleil bowls along at an uncontested, comfortable gallop and the hold-up horses struggle to close ground on the flat Stratford track.
scenarios.body: Duel Au Soleil sets the fractions he wants, Whatyouwaitingfor tracks closely but cannot muster the pace to reel in the leader late on good to firm ground; horses held up in rear find too much ground to make up in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Whatyouwaitingfor travels strongly enough to challenge Duel Au Soleil approaching the final two fences and the front pair pull clear.
scenarios.body: The two prominent types race in tandem throughout, and Whatyouwaitingfor's consistent placed form on similar going — nine runs without falling — sees him find extra in the final exchanges; hold-up horses have no winning angle from well behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Duel Au Soleil sets a stronger-than-expected pace and runs out of fuel in the final half-mile, leaving a closing opportunity.
scenarios.body: The Long Walk, unbeaten in two runs at this sort of trip on good ground when allowed to close late, sweeps through; Hooper's best form has come when pace has collapsed in front of him, and he remains a player at big odds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mary Adapts Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mary's jockey presses forward from the off, reclaims a prominent position and Duel Au Soleil is unable to sustain his effort over 2m3½f.
scenarios.body: Mary has the best course and distance form in the field on similar going — three places from five on good — and if she can override her mapped midfield position early, she has the tactical speed to remain competitive; the strong trainer two-day strike rate from Ian Williams adds a live angle.

watchPoints.text: Watch Duel Au Soleil at the start — if he is slow away or fails to immediately assert at the front, Whatyouwaitingfor may steal a march and turn Scenario A into Scenario B with Duel Au Soleil chasing.

Mary's jockey Charlie Todd may attempt to push forward aggressively from the off to reclaim a prominent position; if successful, she applies pressure to both front-runners earlier than expected and could trigger a tactical contest rather than a controlled procession.

The Long Walk is 43 days off a run for Jonjo O'Neill, whose yard is nonetheless in form (3/13 last 14 days); watch his jumping on the first circuit — any mistakes from a hold-up position on a tight-turning track like Stratford will cost him the ability to close on the leaders.

Good to firm ground at Stratford rewards clean, economical jumping; Hooper's jumping record over fences (including a previous PU in the form string) is worth tracking from the first fence — any hesitancy from Hooper could affect the spacing of the chasing pack behind the leaders.

races.name: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Get A Superstar
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a strong recent record including two wins from last three starts on good ground; front-running style suits an uncontested lead here, Newland & Insole stable in decent 14-day form, and 17 days since last run is fresh enough — the STYLE_FIT tag is nominal as P is very close to L in a small field.

runners_data.name: Stellarmasterpiece
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has placed form across five recent starts on good ground; Sean Bowen is a major asset in terms of positioning and race-reading, and the prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking an uncontested lead in this small field.

runners_data.name: Mystic Wind
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old has shown only modest form with three consecutive finishes of 5-7-7, all on good ground at 16f — this step up to 2m2½f is a query, and no wins or placed runs in three recent starts makes it hard to get enthusiastic despite the powerful yard.

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer whose entire career profile is built around good ground and distances around 16-20f; she holds-up naturally and finishes well but has not converted her placed form into a win in 15 starts on similar going — the value here is as a each-way threat rather than a winner.

runners_data.name: Kotgar
runners_data.note: Handicapper whose true style is hold-up, forced into a midfield mapping by the congestion of rear-runners in this field; modest form (best finish 4th in last five) and a visor in the headgear column suggest connections are trying things — 33 days off is not a concern but the profile is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Ghost Pepper
runners_data.note: David Brace's six-year-old has been off 236 days, carries a form string full of Ps and a pull-up, and has drawn a 5lb claimer from an 0/0 trainer 14-day strike; natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map and hard to recommend with any confidence given the layoff and jumping question marks.

runners_data.name: Hopjes
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a tongue-tie and a form string that includes Unseated, Pulled Up, and 0 in recent outings — three consecutive 7th, 9th, and 11th finishes at 16f suggest this step up to 2m2½f is unlikely to unlock improvement; a natural hold-up runner mapped to midfield by redistribution, and the overall profile is weak.

races.paceDynamic: Get A Superstar is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressers likely to challenge early, will control tempo from the front on Good to Firm ground at Stratford over 2m2½f. Stellarmasterpiece is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and may track up close, but the remainder of the field — Mystic Wind, Northern Rose, Kotgar, Ghost Pepper, and Hopjes — are all hold-up types who will need something to happen late. The field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate in their natural positions; Kotgar, Ghost Pepper, and Hopjes are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the rear of the race is congested and none of them are likely to secure a genuinely comfortable position. With Get A Superstar dictating an uncontested, sustainable gallop, this race shape strongly favours the horse or horses closest to the front who can travel economically and resist a finishing challenge, rewarding prominent racers over closers who will have real ground to make up late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Sets Up
scenarios.trigger: If Get A Superstar dictates an unchallenged, measured pace and Stellarmasterpiece tracks in second throughout.
scenarios.body: Get A Superstar jumps cleanly and rolls along at an honest but not brutal tempo, conserving energy for the final two flights; Stellarmasterpiece sits just off the lead and is ideally placed to pounce if the leader tires, with both prominent profiles well served by the lack of pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to stretch the field and a hold-up runner tracks up powerfully on the final bend.
scenarios.body: A sustained gallop from Get A Superstar strings the field out, creating a clear passage for the best-travelling hold-up horse to pick off rivals in the straight; Northern Rose's consistent placed form on good ground and her excellent record at this trip make her the likeliest beneficiary if the front two tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is so conservative that it becomes a sprint finish off a crawl, negating class and rewarding the sharpest jumper.
scenarios.body: A dawdling pace bunches the field together, removing any advantage from either end of the race and turning the contest on jumping speed and a sprint up the straight; Stellarmasterpiece's recent winning form and Sean Bowen's positional awareness give her an edge in a messy tactical race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Fallers Reshape Race
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or departures among the front two leave a vacuum that a midfield or rear horse can exploit.
scenarios.body: With the field featuring multiple novices and limited jumpers like Ghost Pepper (236 days off, P and F in form) and Hopjes (U and P in form), a significant incident could reshuffle the order entirely; however, none of the redistributed hold-up types carry the class or form to be confident selections even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Get A Superstar at the first flight — if the horse jumps cleanly and crosses to the front unchallenged, the race shape is locked in early and the tactical read becomes straightforward.

Ghost Pepper's 236-day absence combined with a form string containing multiple jumping failures (P and P) makes it a live risk for a jumping error or early departure that could interfere with horses behind.
Hopjes (U, P in form) is a genuine jumping liability under a 7lb claimer; monitor whether it causes interference at the early hurdles given its position in a compressed, hold-up heavy field.

Stellarmasterpiece's jockey Sean Bowen is worth tracking in the early exchanges — if he elects to sit closer to Get A Superstar than expected rather than dropping in, it signals he intends to contest the pace and the shape becomes even more front-two-dominated.

Northern Rose has placed in 6 of 15 starts on similar going without winning — if the pace is strong enough to string the field, she is the most reliable hold-up threat to pick up third or frame money, but watch whether the early tempo is genuinely honest enough to bring her into it.

races.name: Patrick's 60th Celebration Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Campaign Trail
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 26f on Good ground and has placed figures at this trip — the sole confirmed pace-setter here, it will control from the front under Tom Bellamy, though the tongue-tie/cheekpiece combination and its STYLE_FIT tag signal it is stretching into a lead role that may not represent its absolute best.|

runners_data.name: Lion Of The Desert
runners_data.note: In-form horse with back-to-back wins, though all five recent runs have been at 20-22f — stepping up to 2m6f tests an unexplored stamina ceiling; Joe Anderson's 3lb claim is useful and Good/Good-to-Firm going suits, but whether it truly lasts this trip is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Charging Thunder
runners_data.note: Deep hold-up horse who drops dramatically back in trip today — all recent runs at 14-16f and now facing 2m6f on Good to Firm, a surface on which he has one placed effort in 15 attempts; Sean Bowen's quality is an asset but the horse's style and going record make this a big ask.|

runners_data.name: Hillview
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran who has placed form at 24f on Good going, fitted with a hood, though his recent string shows multiple unplaced efforts and a pulled-up; James Bowen rides and the horse has shown he can stay the trip, but a 12-day turnaround and inconsistent form are real caution flags.|

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by nature — shown by a placed effort at 24f on Good ground — but carried into midfield on the race map purely because there are more hold-up types than positions allow; the STYLE_FIT and REDISTRIBUTED tags confirm its true preference is for the rear, which in this gently-run race is not an enviable spot.|

races.paceDynamic: Campaign Trail is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Lion Of The Desert as a genuine second prominent type to apply any pressure, is set to control this race from the front at a sustainable gallop over 2m6f on Good to Firm ground at Stratford. Lion Of The Desert will likely track closely in second, but with neither Charging Thunder, Hillview, nor Parikarma inclined to challenge for the lead, Campaign Trail can dictate terms without being seriously harassed. This creates a steadily-run, attritional shape where the pace is controlled rather than punishing, which suits those who travel prominently and conserve energy over the longer trip. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely come from off the pace in a race run at this measured tempo — Charging Thunder, Hillview, and the redistributed Parikarma all sit in the rear half, meaning closers must produce significant late momentum against horses that have not been softened up. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who travel into the race, particularly those with strong Good to Firm form over this stamina-testing trip, are best positioned to capitalise on a controlled front-running shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Campaign Trail Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Campaign Trail bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable, measured gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Campaign Trail dictates every yard at its own tempo, preserving enough for the final climb; Lion Of The Desert tracks closely but must quicken past a horse that has not been softened up. Prominent types with tactical speed and good form on similar going — particularly Campaign Trail and Lion Of The Desert — are the clear beneficiaries of this dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Lion Of The Desert pushes hard to match Campaign Trail early, creating a genuine pace battle between the two front-rank horses.
scenarios.body: A genuine two-horse duel from the front raises the tempo and tests both, potentially leaving them vulnerable to a fresher challenger sweeping through. Hillview, who has shown composure in similar galloping tracks and has strong distance form, or a late-looming Charging Thunder could capitalise on any over-exertion by the leading pair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to bring hold-up horses into the finish with winning momentum.
scenarios.body: A truly searching pace would allow Charging Thunder or Hillview to close late, though both sit at the back of a small field that is not likely to be run off their feet. This scenario is materially discounted because the true hold-up types — including Parikarma, whose natural rearward style is out of sync with this race shape — are unlikely to generate the finishing burst needed against a well-conserved pace-setter.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Grinds All Out
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Firm ground and 2m6f trip combine to turn the race into a stamina examination that tests every runner.
scenarios.body: A long, grinding finish tests resolution rather than pace, with horses that stay every yard and handle quick ground best surviving. Campaign Trail's headgear (tongue-tie/cheekpieces) and strong form at this distance on Good ground means it retains claims, but Lion Of The Desert's unexplored stamina ceiling at this trip introduces a small doubt.

watchPoints.text: Campaign Trail's uncontested front-running position is the critical race lever — if it gets its own way from the outset, the entire race shape favours it and Lion Of The Desert, and the hold-up contingent may never get competitive.|

Lion Of The Desert's stamina at 2m6f is genuinely untested — if it cannot sustain its effort around the final turn, it opens the door for Hillview or Charging Thunder to mount a late challenge in what is otherwise a thin field.|

Charging Thunder's trip and going profile are both significant concerns — a big hold-up horse with minimal Good to Firm placed efforts tackling a career-long trip for the first time is a combination that demands caution before accepting its chance at face value.|

Parikarma's jockey, Miss Imogen Mathias (7lb claim), is riding a horse that will be pushed out of its natural position — monitor how it settles in the early stages, as discomfort in running style at 7d off its last run could see it detach early and lose contact.|

With only five runners and one genuine pace-setter, any significant incident at a hurdle — particularly in a small, strung-out field on fast ground — could dramatically reshape the finish; Hillview's pulled-up run in recent form is a flag worth noting under a quick turnaround.|

races.name: Silver Fox Classic Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Centara
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls' eight-year-old has solid good-ground form (10/15 sim-going) and arrives 46 days fresh; the confirmed front-runner sets the pace here but recent form reads 21P-64 suggesting slight inconsistency, and racing off a mark of 132 means any error under 166lbs could prove costly.

runners_data.name: Breaking Cover
runners_data.note: Anthony Honeyball in fine 14-day form (2/2) and Sam Twiston-Davies in the saddle gives this prominent runner a strong handler angle; eight runs in similar going yield eight placed efforts (3W6P) and a recent 21-day turnaround suggests freshness, making this horse the most dangerous tracker to Centara.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: An excellent recent record of -11221 and 12/14 sim-going strike rate underlines genuine class, but the six-year-old's naturally prominent style has been squeezed into a midfield mapping by the weight of front-runners in this field, meaning Luke Scott (claiming 3lb) will need to work harder to find the position this horse needs to produce its best.

runners_data.name: In The Air
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 17f on good ground and Ciaran Gethings is a competent partner, but the horse's true front-running preference is effectively blocked by Centara, leaving it to race in a less comfortable midfield berth; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects a meaningful disadvantage in a shape that won't suit its natural aggression.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up runner in the field at age 12, Sean Bowen's mount must close from off the pace on fast ground in a small field — a combination that rarely plays to a closer's strengths; one win from six sim-going runs and a recent P in the form string raise durability questions, though the horse did win last time 21 days ago at OR 122.

races.paceDynamic: Centara is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners over 2m1f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, will dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front with Freddie Gingell unlikely to be challenged for the lead. Breaking Cover is the only other natural prominent runner capable of tracking close to Centara, giving the pace map a clear and relatively thin look at the head of affairs. The field actually contains more prominent-running types than the shape can accommodate — Captain Cool and In The Air are genuine prominent horses by profile but are mapped to midfield because they cannot all hold that position against Centara and Breaking Cover, meaning those two will race in a less natural role. This race shape — a single unchallenged front-runner setting a sustainable gallop on fast ground with a small field — strongly favours prominent and close-tracking profiles, particularly any runner capable of sitting just off Centara and pouncing at the final fence.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centara Dictates, Tracking Horse Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Centara bowls along at a fair but controlled clip and the closest tracker times their challenge perfectly from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Centara sets a sustainable front-running gallop that stretches the modest field without burning them off, leaving the horse in closest attendance with cover and energy reserves to challenge between the last two fences; the fast ground and small field size amplify the advantage of racing close to the pace with minimal traffic to navigate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Centara Outstays All, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Centara is allowed to steal an advantage going out on the final circuit and the field never fully closes the gap.
scenarios.body: Paul Nicholls' eight-year-old, proven on good ground and over this type of trip, converts front-running control into an outright win by simply never being headed; Sean Bowen on Sir Tivo is the only hold-up runner in the field and starts too far back to mount a serious late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool or In The Air push hard for prominent positions early and force a contested, faster-than-ideal tempo.
scenarios.body: A contested front leads to Centara being pressured into burning fuel early on the quick ground, causing a compression of the field as tired horses slow at the final fence; Sir Tivo, the one genuine hold-up runner, is the only horse positioned to capitalise but his age (12) and modest sim-going strike rate make this an unlikely winning formula.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Derails Front Two
scenarios.trigger: If Centara or Breaking Cover make a significant jumping error that gifts momentum to the midfield horses.
scenarios.body: A mid-race blunder from either of the lead pair instantly opens the race up for Captain Cool or In The Air, both of whom are natural prominent horses capable of seizing the front if the race reorganises; both carry STYLE_FIT discounts for running out of role but a jumping incident neutralises that disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Centara jumping cleanly at each fence is the single most important factor — any blunder at the open ditch or down the back straight hands the tactical advantage immediately to Breaking Cover or the redistributed prominent types.

Captain Cool and In The Air may jostle for position in the early stages as both naturally want to race prominently; watch the first two fences for a pace flare-up that could compromise Centara's controlled front-running plan.

Sir Tivo's age (12) and hold-up style in a five-runner field on fast ground leaves Sean Bowen with almost no tactical cover — if the pace is even mildly strong, the closer's ground advantage evaporates before the last.
Breaking Cover's trainer Anthony Honeyball is 2/2 in the 14-day window — a live angle that supports the view this horse arrives primed and ready to make full use of its prominent tracking position.

races.name: PJ McGeever 70th Birthday Celebration Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Artiste d'Ainay
runners_data.note: Billy Aprahamian's yard is firing at 2/2 over the last 14 days and this 8-year-old arrives fresh on a 7-day turnaround having won over course-and-distance equivalent trips on Good; the confirmed pace-setter at OR 98, it carries top weight but is ideally suited to dictating on fast ground.

runners_data.name: East Eagle
runners_data.note: Mike Sowersby's 6-year-old has an excellent profile at this trip and going — 3 wins and 4 places from 15 similar-ground runs — and Charlie Maggs's 3lb claim at OR 87 makes this an interesting each-way proposition tracking the leader in its natural prominent role after 40 days off.

runners_data.name: Luna Run
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's mare won over 26f on Good and holds solid placed form at this trip, but in practice she cannot slot into her preferred position just behind the leaders here given Artiste d'Ainay and East Eagle ahead of her; Megan Fox's 7lb claim is a help, but the forced step back from her natural berth is a real practical disadvantage.

runners_data.name: He Is A Cracker
runners_data.note: Won on his return 16 days ago and has winning hurdles form at 26f on Good, but this 10-year-old is a natural prominent racer who finds himself at the rear simply because the pace pecking order has no room for him further forward — the STYLE_FIT penalty of 0.84 reflects that he is unlikely to replicate his best when unable to race handily.

races.paceDynamic: Artiste d'Ainay is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just four, is virtually guaranteed to set the pace unchallenged from the outset over this stamina-testing 3m2½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Stratford. East Eagle and Luna Run are both natural prominent racers who will track close to the leader, though Luna Run cannot secure that position in a field already stacked with pace-committed types and is effectively racing out of role mapped to midfield. He Is A Cracker, the least pace-committed of the quartet, is similarly displaced — pushed to the rear not because it is a true hold-up horse but because there is nowhere else for it to go in this shape. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position; Artiste d'Ainay and East Eagle are most likely to actually secure their roles. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop on fast ground — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final stages, with no genuine closer likely to produce a late ambush.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Artiste d'Ainay Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Artiste d'Ainay dictates a sustainable gallop and kicks clear before the last flight.
scenarios.body: Artiste d'Ainay, trained by Billy Aprahamian with a 2/2 14-day record and winner over this type of trip and going, sets a measured pace that drains stamina from those tracking it, then quickens decisively. Racing on preferred Good ground with a 7-day turnaround that suggests freshness, it is ideally positioned to run its rivals into the ground before the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: East Eagle Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Artiste d'Ainay's lead proves costly late and East Eagle, tracking closely, asserts from the second-last.
scenarios.body: East Eagle has a strong profile over similar trips and going at this distance band with 3 wins and 4 places from 15 similar-going runs, and Charlie Maggs claims a 3lb allowance that assists in a tight handicap. Tracking the leader throughout, it can exploit any fade by Artiste d'Ainay while racing in its natural prominent position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners burn each other out and He Is A Cracker, effectively held up, picks up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: He Is A Cracker has winning form at 26f and returns here on 16 days' rest with a recent course win in its form string, and Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim helps the weight burden. However, this scenario depends on a horse that is a natural prominent type racing genuinely held up — a shape it has not naturally adopted — which materially reduces confidence in this outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Luna Run Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Luna Run, despite being mapped out of its prominent role, settles mid-division and produces a sustained staying run to collar them all.
scenarios.body: Luna Run won over 26f on Good ground and handles this surface well, but is racing out of its preferred prominent position here given the competition for early berths, which compromises its chance significantly. Megan Fox's 7lb claim mitigates the weight disadvantage slightly, but this scenario is a low-probability outcome precisely because the horse cannot race as it would ideally want.

watchPoints.text: Artiste d'Ainay sets the pace unchallenged — watch whether James Bowen elects to go very early and build a substantial lead or instead adopts a steadier, energy-conserving gallop, as the tempo choice will shape every other runner's race.

East Eagle is the most natural beneficiary if Artiste d'Ainay weakens late — watch its jumping and positioning from the second circuit onwards to gauge whether Charlie Maggs can close the gap approaching the final hurdle.

Luna Run's ability to secure a forward position at the first bend is key — if she is shuffled back early, the style disadvantage compounds throughout this 3m2½f trip and her chance diminishes rapidly.

He Is A Cracker has a recent winning run on the board but his forcing style is neutered in this shape; watch whether Isabelle Ryder attempts to push forward early or accepts a rearward berth, as the former could cause interference while the latter hands a significant advantage to the confirmed pace-setters.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this race — all four runners are rated OK on the going, but over 3m2½f on a flat Stratford track, fast conditions will amplify the advantage of the front-runner if it can control the tempo without overextending early.

races.name: Grace And Dotty Conditional Jockeys' Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Basilette
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good recent form — a winner 7 days ago and with two wins at similar trips on Good going — sits ideal just off the pace at OR 99 and wears headgear; the short turnaround is worth monitoring but Jeff Mullins has been running her frequently and she appears in good order.

runners_data.name: Roarin' Success
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's mare ran well on a recent return to winning ways 20 days ago (OR 101), but her true hold-up style asks questions in a race where the pace is unlikely to be fierce enough to set her up; William Maggs claims 3lb but this shape may not play to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Lucy The Wire
runners_data.note: Sole front runner in the field and confirmed pace-setter; tagged with a style-fit flag of 0.92 reflecting that she may not fully dominate at this trip on quicker ground — her record on Good is solid (5/7) but James Owen's filly has to do it all from the front with no cover whatsoever.

runners_data.name: Klervia
runners_data.note: A hold-up mare whose best form has come at 20f-23f on Good ground, suggesting this 18½f trip may be on the short side; Isabelle Ryder takes the ride for F Brennan (1 winner from 3 in 14 days) but a 30-day break and a modest recent form string including a pull-up temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Dusky Spyglass
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up type returning after a 130-day absence with a modest form string including two pull-ups, and Mike Murphy has had 0 winners from 5 in the past 14 days; positioned in midfield on the map because the rear is congested, but her true running style is from off the pace — the absence and form make her a significant risk regardless of race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Lucy The Wire is the sole confirmed front runner in this five-runner mares' handicap hurdle and, with no genuine rival to press her early, she should set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Stratford. Basilette is the natural prominent challenger but sits at OR 99 and will likely track rather than challenge for the lead, leaving Lucy The Wire to dictate terms unchallenged through the early stages. Dusky Spyglass is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is already occupied by Roarin' Success and Klervia, meaning her natural late-running position is squeezed — she is unlikely to operate from her preferred spot. This shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter on a fair surface with no pressure — strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader at a comfortable clip and kick when challenged, rather than hold-up types who will need a genuine pace collapse that is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lucy The Wire Leads Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Lucy The Wire takes the front unchallenged and sets a measured, controlled pace that suits a prominent tracker finishing strongly.
scenarios.body: Lucy The Wire dictates from the front on ground she handles well, keeping the tempo honest enough to stay in contention herself at the finish; any prominent horse travelling fluidly just off the leader is perfectly placed to pounce at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Overwhelms
scenarios.trigger: If Basilette travels powerfully just off Lucy The Wire and has enough in reserve to collar her between the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Basilette, who has winning form at this trip on Good ground and wears headgear, is ideally placed to exploit a front runner who has done all the work; her recent win over 18f on Good gives her the class edge in this small field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lucy The Wire's pace proves faster than it appears, stringing the field out and leaving genuine closers with enough ground to make up late.
scenarios.body: Roarin' Success, a hold-up type with a recent winning run on Good ground, would be the beneficiary if the front-runners tie each other up over the final mile; however, Donald McCain's mare needs a stronger gallop than this race is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse and Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Lucy The Wire sets a genuinely strong pace and weakens sharply late, handing the race to whichever survivor is best placed.
scenarios.body: With only five runners and a single pace-setter, a full pace collapse is the least likely outcome, but Klervia's best form at longer trips on Good ground gives her an outside chance if stamina becomes the dominant factor.

watchPoints.text: Lucy The Wire faces no pace pressure at all — watch whether she exploits this by stretching the field early, which would expose the hold-up horses immediately.

Dusky Spyglass returns after 130 days and her jumping should be monitored closely in the early stages — a mistake or stumble in a five-runner field on fast ground could have an outsized impact on race shape.
Basilette runs just seven days after her last start — watch for any signs of fatigue in the latter stages if she has to work hard tracking an uncontested front runner.

The Good to Firm surface (confirmed for this race) is faster than the declared Good in the race conditions — horses whose form reads well on genuinely Good ground but who haven't been tested on faster turf should be assessed with caution, particularly Klervia and Roarin' Success.
